subject.title: [Bug]: Concurrent allow-always approvals silently lose allowlist entries (last-write-wins race in exec-approvals.json)

question: Should maintainers adopt or replace the shared guarded-write/CAS fix path for exec approval stale writes, or sponsor a narrower allow-always-only fix for this issue?
rationale: The bug affects a host command-execution approval boundary and overlaps an open security-sensitive PR, so automation should not choose the persistence contract or create another fix branch without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt or replace the shared guarded-write fix
options.body: Use the existing guarded-write/CAS direction, refreshed on current main, to cover allow-always and usage metadata writeback together before closing this issue.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow allow-always fix
options.body: Limit the repair to concurrent allow-always persistence if maintainers want to defer the broader execution metadata security fix.

options.title: Wait for the security PR track
options.body: Keep this issue open until the node stale-writeback security fix decides the shared persistence primitive.

recommendation.title: Adopt or replace the shared guarded-write fix
recommendation.body: Use the existing guarded-write/CAS direction, refreshed on current main, to cover allow-always and usage metadata writeback together before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent exec approval persistence and release-history work is closest to the shared guarded-write boundary under review.
